transcript: One of the first things you learn when you start playing is the value of the pieces. The pawn is worth one point. The knight is worth [music] three points and the same value applies to the bishop. And one of the things that you are told very early on is to be very careful not to lose your queen because the queen is worth nine points. And so just like that, we get very scared and very worried about losing our queen. And what is so beautiful and special about that is the fact that very often the next thing you learn is how to give up your queen. This is seemingly counter-intuitive. One queen is worth three times one bishop and that is true. But at the end of the day, we are always reminded that the goal of the game is to get to the king. And just like that, chess teaches us that sometimes sacrifices are not only necessary but they are the only path to achieve victory.
